threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the underground.' The locals just roll their eyes; it's a dead giveaway.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week and overheard a couple debating the best jellied eels in London. Their passion was unreal; they were serious about their eel rankings.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found that little bakery on Weserstraße, the one with the best pistachio croissants, always a line out the door.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 3 AM from a stand where the guys are still arguing about football while serving you. It’s a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate BART delays—while newcomers panic at the Civic Center exit, we just roll our eyes and grab a burrito.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy balancing on a skateboard while holding a bouquet of flowers and reading a book on the 31 while everyone else stared at their phones.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we all embrace the 'quirky' architecture, but locals just see the endless maintenance bills piling up on those Gaudí-inspired facades.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll notice them looking at the metro map like it's a treasure map, while the locals swipe past effortlessly. Classic giveaway.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You asked for directions to the train station and said 'the Tube' instead of just 'the Overground'; you can spot a newcomer a mile away.
Caught a Brixton night bus last week, and a guy tried to barter with the driver for a free ride using a packet of biscuits. Didn't work, but it was oddly entertaining.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw two kids playing with a stray cat outside the Kiez-Kiosk while their parents debated the football score over a beer. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a hidden bar behind a laundromat that serves cocktails from thrifted teapots. It's a vibe you won't get anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they can name all the taco trucks along Mission without missing a beat, while the newbies still ask for a fancy sit-down.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a guy juggling on the 47, while a lady argued with her grocery bags about a missing apple. Classic Muni chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think 'Gràcia' is just Gaudí and rooftop bars, but it’s really about the neighborhood festivals and the local artists crafting their stories on every street.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they ask for a 'tapa' instead of simply ordering food; locals know it's all about sharing, not just snacks.
